content.introduction: Big tech companies, including Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Google, experienced a significant market value loss after a sharp rise in their AI spending in the third quarter, turning some of their most profitable businesses into cash incinerators. Anthropic, on the other hand, announced significant cost reductions for its AI models, with a 40 to 60% reduction in costs for its latest model, and employees hired in 2026 could expect compensation ranging from $10 to $20 million. Despite these cost reductions, Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, raising concerns about its financial health as it prepares for an IPO.

Anthropic picked a tough week to unveil its IPO prospectus.

Within days of its release, several of the company's key partners, including Microsoft, Google and Amazon, reported quarterly results that added fuel to existing market jitters around the artificial intelligence buildout. [...] Microsoft, Google and Amazon all had notes of concern this week in their reports. The companies have been on a spending blitz in recent years to meet the surge in demand for AI infrastructure, but all three issued capex figures or forecasts that came in below analysts' estimates. Microsoft lowered its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, while Alphabet maintained its guidance for up to $205 billion and Amazon reiterated its roughly $220 billion forecast. [...] Heading into this week, fears were mounting about the financial health of neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, which are facing rising borrowing costs and a dearth of lenders as they pursue aggressive AI buildouts. Anthropic gets much of its capacity from Amazon, Google and SpaceX, but it also relies on neoclouds for some compute as it races to expand as quickly as possible.

Now investors are growing increasingly worried about the whole AI trade.

ClaudeAI charge $100/month for their pretty good plan, in order for Anthropic to become profitable they need to increase that price to a little over $4000/month. Just wait until so many businesses become so dependent on it that they don't have a choice but to pay.

This has been the AI financial strategy for the last 2 years and it's playing out perfectly, more and more people are leaning on AI features every day.
